A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the BAH dataset and its recognition benchmarks. Their main text, appendices, tables and figures support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and revised experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset statistics and supervised, zero-shot and domain-adaptation experiments in Section 4 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 reports revised recognition experiments, dataset analyses, annotator-agreement measurements and a repeated-seed visual-feature comparison.

M1.justification: The core collection procedure, binary annotation scheme and existing learning, fusion and adaptation procedures are retained. Expanded annotation descriptions disclose details rather than establish procedural changes. The head-pose comparison evaluates an additional baseline; Section 4's two-level conflict-recognition framework is future-work guidance.

E1.justification: The represented age range expands from 18–66 to 18–74 years, a limited population extension confirmed by Figure 8 in both versions. The nine Canadian provinces, English/French recordings, seven prompts, pretraining datasets and recognition tasks remain covered.

E2.justification: v3 adds a comparison using TokenHPE-derived head-pose features against cropped-face and full-frame baselines in Appendix I.1/Table 15. The existing ResNet/APViT, modality-fusion, Video-LLaVA and domain-adaptation comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: BAH expands from 1,118 to 1,427 videos, with participant splits changing from 143/25/56 to 195/30/75 and newly stated demographic matching. Benchmark tables replace positive-class F1 and weighted F1 with unweighted AVGF1. The main default backbone changes from ResNet152 to ResNet101, the context ablation changes backbone and stated window range, and UDA batch size changes from 128 to 64.

E4.justification: v3 adds annotator-agreement checks, split-demographic analyses, extensive cue-frequency/co-occurrence analyses and a cropped-face/full-frame/head-pose ablation. Context and demographic performance analyses are revised. The detailed individual-participant adaptation analysis is removed, and Figure 21 omits the 18–24 and 55–64 age-group results shown in v1 Figure 13.

E5.justification: v3 Table 15 newly reports means and standard deviations over five repetitions with different seeds for the visual-feature comparison. Section 2.1 adds Fleiss's kappa estimation on ten multiply annotated videos. These practices have limited coverage; domain-adaptation means and standard deviations across participants were already reported in v1.

E6.justification: Supervised, zero-shot and adaptation result tables are extensively replaced, new agreement/cue/visual-feature results are added, and per-participant adaptation results are removed. For example, the highest multimodal frame-level AP changes from visual+audio at 0.2818 in v1 Table 6 to audio+text at 0.2609 in v3 Table 5. Changed data and backbone settings prevent interpreting this as a same-setting performance decline.

T1.justification: Neither version presents theoretical results or proofs. The annotation codebook's substantive definitions are retained, and the evaluation-metric substitution and expanded conceptual explanations introduce no new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the first BAH dataset and preliminary recognition benchmarks. v3 adds explicit claims that collection mirrors real-world digital interventions and emphasizes within-modality conflict alongside cross-modal conflict, strengthening the stated need for specialized fusion and temporal modelling.

C2.justification: v3 develops substantial interpretations of cue statistics and proposes a two-level future framework for recognizing affect conflicts. It adds explanations concerning binary labels, absence of an annotation apex, geographic generalizability and background noise in full-frame inputs. The limitations section is relocated, but v1's annotation-reliability and annotator-expectation bias paragraph is removed.

D1.justification: v3 documents annotator training, uncertainty resolution and the annotation workflow, clarifies that self-ratings are not labels, and describes frozen TokenHPE feature extraction. Figure 4 newly lists frame-extraction scripts and version information. Conversely, v1 Table 23's participant identifiers and detailed adaptation split counts disappear. Most existing preprocessing, hardware and credentialed-access information remains.

R1.justification: v3 adds seven references, including Fleiss on agreement, TokenHPE, personalized feature translation, sentiment analysis and behavioural research. The earlier reference coverage and first-A/H-dataset positioning largely persist. Moving related work to Appendix A and updating publication metadata do not constitute additional substantive positioning changes.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten, annotation explanations expand, and a recommendations section is introduced. Related work and limitations move from the main text to Appendices A and B, with extensive appendix reorganization. The title adds 'Digital', alongside terminology and language edits.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column layout with a boxed opening to a two-column layout, with widespread resizing and relocation of displays. New demographic and cue figures and a visual-feature table are added; metric columns and context plots are restructured. Four detailed participant-level adaptation tables are removed.

improvement.justification: The new agreement study partly addresses v1's acknowledged annotation-reliability gap, while repeated-seed visual ablations and cue/split analyses improve dataset characterization. The net gain is limited: agreement covers only ten videos, detailed personalization splits/results are removed, and some revised descriptions remain unreconciled—for example, Appendix I.2 discusses WF1/F1 although Figure 20 reports AVGF1/AP.
